hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County. The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, stating "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" warranting his removal.

In her order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. Theobald told WPTV the case raises questions about where lines are drawn for teachers speaking outside school. The school board retains final authority on reinstatement, with no timeline announced for a decision.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking governor
cards.teaser: Multiple anonymous social media accounts were deactivated Friday after prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team accused Layla Collins, w.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were deactivated after allegations connected them to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. Communications specialists from Governor Ron DeSantis' team accused her of operating the accounts to attack the governor and promote her husband's gubernatorial campaign. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, shared evidence linking the accounts to Layla Collins. Promota CEO Robert Salvador posted information showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to known contact information for Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, which showed an access attempt triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits showing. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that also appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw said the account content was entirely comprised of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. She noted that Layla Collins was appointed to a state board by DeSantis. Redfern stated the FSUdude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number. After Pushaw and Redfern made their accusations public, both accounts were deactivated. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby as Fourth of July boaters hit the water
cards.teaser: Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said they are expecting hundreds of boaters to be on the water celebrating this weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are hitting the waterways across Florida to celebrate the Fourth of July weekend. On Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County, boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water.

Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said they're expecting hundreds of boaters to be on the water celebrating this weekend. His team will have two boats with medics on standby in Martin County in the north and south. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, have a designated driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Secretary of State seeks to block St. Cloud Republican from ballot after last-minute filing error
cards.teaser: Paula Stark submitted incomplete qualifying paperwork less than 30 minutes before the June 12 deadline. Five state employees said her treasurer never submitted the required Form 6.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to keep Paula Stark off the ballot for House District 47 after the St. Cloud Republican failed to properly submit required paperwork. In response to Stark's lawsuit seeking ballot access, Byrd's office argues that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, to state employees. Nor was the form accidentally handed back when Davis submitted other paperwork in the final hour of the qualifying window on June 12. Stark's incomplete materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline. Five state employees provided sworn written court declarations supporting the state's position that the form was never received.

Byrd said in his court response that Stark and Davis could have avoided this situation through basic care and caution. Had they questioned why the Form 6 was allegedly handed back, or had Davis not waited until the last minute to submit the documents, the missing form could have been caught and corrected before the deadline. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve noted that Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly submit Form 6, but half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Three weeks after the qualifying deadline, Stark still has not submitted the form. Without seeing it, Reeve said, the state cannot review whether Stark would have met qualification requirements.

Reeve's court filing also detailed a pattern of problems with Stark's campaign paperwork over multiple election cycles. Davis has filed campaign finance reports more than a month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. In 2022 and 2024, audits found inconsistent fund transfers and balance issues. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November due to more than 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. A late report fine that was upheld by the Florida Elections Commission went unpaid and was referred to debt collection in November 2025.

The stakes are significant. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 becomes open to all voters to decide between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republicans filed to run in the traditionally blue House District representing Osceola and Orange counties. Byrd emphasized the tight timeline, noting that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4 and vote-by-mail ballots are scheduled to go out July 9-16. The Universal Primary Contest for House District 47 is already underway, and reversing course would be costly and likely create confusion, according to Byrd's filing.

cards.headline: Lightning strike kills beachgoer in Florida
cards.teaser: A beachgoer died after being struck by lightning while swimming in Florida. Witnesses described the sound as resembling an atomic bomb.
cards.body:
A person was killed by a lightning strike while swimming at a Florida beach, according to reports. The New York Post reported that witnesses described the sound of the strike as resembling an atomic bomb going off. The incident occurred as Fourth of July celebrations were beginning across the state.

Lightning strikes remain a significant weather hazard in Florida, particularly during the summer months when afternoon thunderstorms are common. The state experiences some of the highest rates of lightning activity in the United States. The fatality occurred during a period of active weather as holiday weekend activities were underway at beaches statewide.

hero.headline: Juno Beach residents push for new fence at JB-7 beach access as town faces thousands in costs
hero.teaser: A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating tension between Colony Condos residents and summer beachgoers, with a fix potentially costing the town thousands of dollars.
hero.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos are seeking town help to reinstall a fence at the JB-7 public beach access point, saying beachgoers have been trespassing on their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. The barrier that once clearly marked the boundary between public walkway and private land has been replaced only by shrubs, leaving condo owners frustrated with increased foot traffic and vehicle parking on their property during the busy summer months.

Lori Hill, a resident at the condominiums, described how the absence of the fence has led to regular incidents of people cutting through private land with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs to access the beach. Hill said these trespassers also park in spots reserved for residents. The situation has escalated to the point where residents no longer confront people directly about being on private property, instead calling police to handle the encounters. Hill said the problem is particularly severe during summer season when beach traffic increases significantly.

Not all observers see the fence removal as problematic. Michael House, a beachgoer who walks to JB-7 from a public parking lot nearby, said he has not witnessed the trespassing and vehicle issues residents describe. He noted that ample free parking is available in the area and questioned whether property damage or littering represents the real concern rather than people crossing the boundary.

When the matter came before the Juno Beach Town Council, officials clarified that the town has no legal obligation to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring more affordable alternatives, proposing that the town might help fund a lower-cost fence option or combine split rail fencing with additional shrubs to create a clearer boundary. The council decided to address the fence question during its budget discussions scheduled for July 15. Hill expressed hope that town officials will take action to restore the fence, allowing residents to reclaim their landscaping areas and parking spaces.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, and the only Florida city selected this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach is celebrating its selection as the only Florida city among 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The award was announced at the National Civic League conference in Denver, recognizing communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, stating "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through long-term efforts to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic engagement programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive 'A' rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an 'A' rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
For the third year in a row, the School District of Palm Beach County received an "A" rating from the state, a streak district leaders attribute to strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, earned "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5 percent graduation rate, and 86 percent of seniors participated in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the district's biggest success stories came from S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which improved from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served in that role for 15 years, led the turnaround by fine-tuning the school's academic approach and raising expectations across campus. The school modified its early childhood curriculum program, which serves children starting at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from "C" to "A" this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denial hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: A breast cancer patient and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter, the FDA stated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is less risky than other options with proven success. Billington has joined doctors taking their frustrations to social media and calling out insurers by name. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem's spokesperson stated the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy." Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex a little more than a week ago.

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned an invitation to march in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4 at 10:30 a.m., representing Florida at the prestigious event. The students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the magnitude of the moment, noting that millions of people will be watching. "It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion," she said. Senior Stephin Restivo emphasized the team's focus on precision, saying "Everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of." Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying "I have full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, noting it showcases how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those watching from home.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4 percent this year
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago. The survey attributes the increase to inflation, with ground beef prices rising 5.5 percent and buns up 7.7 percent. Strawberries have been hit particularly hard by a Florida frost, jumping 12.4 percent in price, while ice cream costs have risen 5.3 percent.

Not all food items have become more expensive this year. Potato prices are down, benefiting those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends comparing stores to find the best deals on groceries and using a meal plan to cut down on food waste.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of their belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a house fire Monday in Hobe Sound. Investigators from the sheriff's office believe an electrical issue may have caused the blaze, though the fire remains under investigation. White's fiancé, Mark, survived the incident, but the flames destroyed much of their home and belongings.

Friends learned of White's death when Mark called to share the tragic news. Nina Fenn, who had known White for eight years, spoke about the loss and visited the scene in the days following the fire to process her grief. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said. The community has rallied around Mark by launching a fundraiser to help him rebuild his life after losing his home and possessions in the fire.

Fenn described White as someone who made a lasting impression on those around her. White was a Christian woman who enjoyed gardening, plants, and playing piano. According to Fenn, "She was always the first to lend a hand." White also had a deep love for children and people in general. Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her, noting, "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts."

The timing of White's death compounds the tragedy for those close to her. Her birthday was July 4th, meaning she passed away just days before turning a year older. The loss is especially difficult for Mark, who has already endured significant personal tragedy. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. "So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him." As the community supports Mark through this devastating time, White's loved ones remember her for the kindness and joy she brought to their lives.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with his comments, which labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

cards.headline: Juno Beach residents want fence restored at JB-7 beach access point as trespassing complaints mount
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. A fix could cost the town thousands of dollars.
cards.body:
A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating tension between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with a potential fix costing the town thousands of dollars. Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer, with cars parking randomly and beachgoers pushing back bushes to access the area with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Hill said residents used to confront trespassers directly but have increasingly turned to calling police after encountering rudeness.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring lower-cost solutions. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. Hill expressed hope that the town would restore the fence to protect landscaping and private parking. The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between current Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. The interchange aims to improve accessibility and accommodate growth in Port St. Lucie over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. Crews are currently in the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial Turnpike interchange is also still in the design phase. The project will include bike and pedestrian paths as well as sidewalks. The city council will vote on final approval to transfer the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County to consider elevated autonomous transit connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
A California-based autonomous transit company is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. Glydways, which has projects underway in Atlanta and California, will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect the airport to the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned for the system because major transportation hubs already exist close together but are not easily connected for pedestrians or travelers. He pointed to increasing congestion along Okeechobee Boulevard, Southern Boulevard and Belvedere Road. While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. He referenced previous South Florida light rail discussions with estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County deputies make 15 DUI arrests in impaired driving operation
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County deputies targeted impaired driving in a recent operation that resulted in 15 DUI arrests.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County deputies made 15 DUI arrests as part of a recent operation targeting impaired driving in the county. The arrests come as law enforcement agencies across Florida increase patrols during the Fourth of July holiday weekend.

Authorities have emphasized the dangers of driving under the influence, particularly during holiday periods when traffic volumes increase. The operation reflects ongoing efforts by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office to keep roads safe for residents and visitors.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has earned a major national recognition as one of only 10 communities selected nationwide for the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city stands as the sole Florida recipient of this honor. The award was presented during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where city leaders showcased their efforts to build stronger community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the achievement, stating that "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson attributed the award to years of work aimed at revitalizing the city and improving residents' quality of life.

The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, recognizes communities that unite residents, local government, businesses and organizations to address challenges and create meaningful change. City leaders emphasized that the recognition reflects a long-term commitment to improving civic health, rebuilding trust between residents and government, and enabling the community to directly shape the city's future. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the accomplishment, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents. Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs that demonstrate civic participation and community investment. The Riviera Beach Youth Council engages high school students in civic leadership and advocacy work. The Citizens Leadership Academy provides civic education with a 98% completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program offers mini-grants to longtime homeowners for necessary repairs. Miller-Anderson noted that these initiatives represent the city's commitment to treating civic engagement as a partnership involving government, residents, faith groups, schools and community organizations. She emphasized that the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride.

City officials view the All-America City designation as a significant statement to the nation about Riviera Beach's character and future potential. The honor positions the community for continued growth and new opportunities while demonstrating that collaboration produces results. The recognition validates what residents have observed during years of change and revitalization efforts throughout the city. The other nine communities receiving the 2026 award are Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a fire at her Hobe Sound home on Monday. The sheriff's office determined a possible electrical issue caused the fire, which remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of their belongings.

Nina Fenn, who has been White's friend for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people," Fenn said. The loss carries added weight for Mark, who previously lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's death is particularly heartbreaking because she passed just days before her birthday on July 4th.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended following social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, contending that numerous findings are not based upon competent substantial evidence. The board's attorney maintains that Theobald's Facebook post, which labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, constituted a serious offense warranting his removal.

Livingstone's order cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. Theobald told WPTV the case raises broader questions about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. The school board retains final authority over whether Theobald returns to his position.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% as inflation hits ground beef, strawberries
cards.teaser: A holiday cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation as the cause. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%. Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said there are ways to keep costs in check. "It's really important to shop savvier than ever, it is comparing the stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list, the biggest thing for families is cutting down the food waste, and that begins with a meal plan," Woroch said. Several Treasure Coast shoppers described their Fourth of July meal plans Friday. One shopper said they are having hamburgers with coleslaw, chips and maybe some beer for lunch, and some burnt ends, mashed potatoes and fresh broccoli for dinner. Another shopper said they cook hamburgers, beef, steak and baked potato.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction hours before surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her reconstruction surgery denied by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before it was scheduled because the surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and planned a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction using GalaFlex, a synthetic surgical mesh. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage, stating the procedure was "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is popular among plastic surgeons and FDA-approved for some uses in the body, but it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. Billington has publicly criticized insurance denials on social media. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week later thanks to Billington's efforts. Anthem responded that it regularly reviews coverage policies based on medical evidence and that the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial. Last year, Cigna became the first major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction following investigative reporting.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated network connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations using small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays or intermediate stops. Travel times would be seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. The elevated guideway would resemble a narrow pedestrian bridge, with stations potentially integrated into buildings to shield riders from weather.

Gettinger noted that West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned for the system because major transportation hubs already exist close together but lack easy connections for pedestrians or travelers. He cited increasing congestion along Okeechobee Boulevard, Southern Boulevard and Belvedere Road as evidence the region needs new transportation solutions. While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of traditional light rail, which carries South Florida estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's meeting would determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal rather than approve construction.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football aims for state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are preparing for the 2026 fall football season with ambitious goals after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. Despite their success, a second-round playoff loss has motivated the team to reach higher. The squad is using summer workouts as a stepping stone toward a state title run.

Head football coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of this year's senior class as a key advantage for the program. Most of the seniors have been with the school for four years, having come through the middle school program. Robertson said many of these players have already experienced success during their time at Saint Andrew's, and he believes their senior season has the potential to be the best in program history. This veteran leadership provides a solid foundation for the team's ambitious goals.

To challenge themselves and elevate their program, the Scots are taking on a more demanding schedule this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained that the team deliberately chose to compete against quality opponents to push themselves to the next level. Playing stronger teams will not only help the program improve but also draw attention from other athletes who want to be part of a competitive program. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that while going undefeated would be nice, the real measure of success this season is advancing further in the playoffs. He noted that regular season perfection means little if the team continues to lose in the second round of postseason play. The focus is on playoff performance above all else.

The players are embracing the daily commitment required to reach their goals. Senior Edmyer St. Jean described summer workouts as something the team looks forward to, viewing the daily grind as an investment in future results. The mentality throughout the program centers on working harder now so that the team can finish the season on a positive note and break their previous records. As the Scots prepare for the upcoming season, their combination of experienced leadership, a challenging schedule, and a commitment to improvement positions them as a team determined to go deeper into the playoffs and compete for a state championship.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby as Fourth of July boaters hit the water
cards.teaser: Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said they are expecting hundreds of boaters to be on the water celebrating this weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are hitting the waterways across Florida to celebrate the Fourth of July weekend. On Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County, boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water.

Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said they're expecting hundreds of boaters to be on the water celebrating this weekend. His team will have two boats with medics on standby in Martin County in the north and south. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, have a designated driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets relief after lien removed and roof fixed when WPTV steps in
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran, came to WPTV after months of frustration with a roofing contractor he said left him with unfinished repairs and a lien on his home.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, needed to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season and hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach after seeing them frequently in his neighborhood. He made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000 and was mostly satisfied with the work, except for two holes left unfinished on the back of his home. When the company stopped responding, McCoy called, texted and emailed repeatedly between January 10 and February 5, when a worker finally responded saying the owner would call. The owner never called back.

Letters from Gulfeagle Supply then arrived warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien on McCoy's home for unpaid materials supplied to Seabreeze Roofing. McCoy worried he would need to hire an attorney. After a WPTV investigative reporter spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, McCoy received a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized within an hour. The contractor also agreed to send someone back to fix the two problem areas. About an hour after McCoy received the waiver, he sent WPTV a photo showing crews finishing the roof repairs.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie works to expand Midway Road and add Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange.
cards.body:
Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. Samples said the interchange is all about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," said Samples.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, which remains in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths, along with sidewalks. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to FDOT to assist with the interchange. City council will vote on final approval at an upcoming meeting.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County. The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle programs through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these seasonal experiences are designed to help visitors learn about sea turtle conservation on one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. During educational demonstrations, visitors may see red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment in use. Loggerhead Marinelife Center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Secretary of State seeks to block St. Cloud Republican from ballot after last-minute filing error
hero.teaser: Paula Stark submitted incomplete qualifying paperwork less than 30 minutes before the June 12 deadline. Five state employees said her treasurer never submitted the required Form 6.
hero.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to keep Paula Stark off the ballot for House District 47 after the St. Cloud Republican failed to properly submit required paperwork. In response to Stark's lawsuit seeking ballot access, Byrd's office argues that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, to state employees. Nor was the form accidentally handed back when Davis submitted other paperwork in the final hour of the qualifying window on June 12. Stark's incomplete materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline. Five state employees provided sworn written court declarations supporting the state's position that the form was never received.

Byrd said in his court response that Stark and Davis could have avoided this situation through basic care and caution. Had they questioned why the Form 6 was allegedly handed back, or had Davis not waited until the last minute to submit the documents, the missing form could have been caught and corrected before the deadline. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve noted that Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly submit Form 6, but half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Three weeks after the qualifying deadline, Stark still has not submitted the form. Without seeing it, Reeve said, the state cannot review whether Stark would have met qualification requirements.

Reeve's court filing also detailed a pattern of problems with Stark's campaign paperwork over multiple election cycles. Davis has filed campaign finance reports more than a month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. In 2022 and 2024, audits found inconsistent fund transfers and balance issues. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November due to more than 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. A late report fine that was upheld by the Florida Elections Commission went unpaid and was referred to debt collection in November 2025.

The stakes are significant. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 becomes open to all voters to decide between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republicans filed to run in the traditionally blue House District representing Osceola and Orange counties. Byrd emphasized the tight timeline, noting that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4 and vote-by-mail ballots are scheduled to go out July 9-16. The Universal Primary Contest for House District 47 is already underway, and reversing course would be costly and likely create confusion, according to Byrd's filing.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking governor
cards.teaser: Multiple anonymous social media accounts were deactivated Friday after prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team accused Layla Collins, w.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were deactivated after allegations connected them to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. Communications specialists from Governor Ron DeSantis' team accused her of operating the accounts to attack the governor and promote her husband's gubernatorial campaign. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, shared evidence linking the accounts to Layla Collins. Promota CEO Robert Salvador posted information showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to known contact information for Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, which showed an access attempt triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits showing. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that also appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw said the account content was entirely comprised of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. She noted that Layla Collins was appointed to a state board by DeSantis. Redfern stated the FSUdude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number. After Pushaw and Redfern made their accusations public, both accounts were deactivated. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site around civic park and museum
cards.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid proposal featuring 3,600 income-restricted housing units, a 13-acre central park, and a permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid as the city's preferred plan for redeveloping Tropicana Field and the surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, the $8.1 billion proposal calls for purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million. The team values the full land package at $405 million when factoring in $130 million in land the city would retain, and proposes a $20 million deposit when a purchase and sale agreement is executed. Unlike previous redevelopment plans centered on a new stadium, The Burg Bid would be organized around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre central park designed as a civic and cultural space. The park would be part of 18.5 acres of public park space and include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a planned Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, cafe areas, public art and a concert lawn. A surf wave attraction, recreation deck, multimodal hub, workforce and small-business center, and Resilience Event Center are also planned.

The proposal calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The plan includes homeownership opportunities at a discount to market value. The district would be built in three main phases lasting about five years each, with early development possible outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. The team's lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: Lightning strike kills beachgoer in Florida
cards.teaser: A beachgoer died after being struck by lightning while swimming in Florida. Witnesses described the sound as resembling an atomic bomb.
cards.body:
A person was killed by a lightning strike while swimming at a Florida beach, according to reports. The New York Post reported that witnesses described the sound of the strike as resembling an atomic bomb going off. The incident occurred as Fourth of July celebrations were beginning across the state.

Lightning strikes remain a significant weather hazard in Florida, particularly during the summer months when afternoon thunderstorms are common. The state experiences some of the highest rates of lightning activity in the United States. The fatality occurred during a period of active weather as holiday weekend activities were underway at beaches statewide.

cards.teaser: Rescue crews pulled two people from the water after their boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
Two boaters were rescued from the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County after their vessel sank. Emergency responders arrived on scene to pull the individuals from the water.

Bodycam footage captured the rescue operation as crews worked to save the two people. Both individuals were safely recovered from the waterway following the sinking incident.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman honored for Little Free Library support
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce resident received recognition for her work supporting little free libraries in the community.
cards.body:
A woman from Fort Pierce was recognized for her efforts in supporting little free libraries throughout the area. The recognition highlights her contributions to promoting literacy and book access in the community.

Little free libraries provide neighborhood book exchanges where residents can take and share books freely. The Fort Pierce woman's support has helped expand these community resources.

cards.headline: Costco planning first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: The warehouse retailer Costco is planning to open its first store on the Treasure Coast in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Costco has announced plans to open a store in Port St. Lucie, marking the first location for the warehouse chain on the Treasure Coast. The new store will bring the membership-based retailer to St. Lucie County.

The Port St. Lucie Costco will provide area residents access to bulk groceries, household goods, and other merchandise. This represents the company's entry into the Treasure Coast market after serving other parts of Florida.

cards.headline: Legacy Lions football team standings updated for Port St. Lucie high school
cards.teaser: Current football standings have been released for the Legacy Lions at Legacy High School in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
The Legacy Lions football team from Port St. Lucie has updated standings for the season. Legacy High School's football program continues its competitive season with current rankings now available.

The standings provide Port St. Lucie residents with information about the local high school team's performance. Legacy High School serves students in the Port St. Lucie area.

hero.headline: Juno Beach residents push for fence replacement at JB-7 beach access as costs could reach thousands
hero.body:
Residents at Colony Condos in Juno Beach are concerned about trespassers crossing their private property since the town removed a boundary fence in 2023 for safety reasons. With only bushes now separating the public beach walkway from private land, condo owners say beachgoers are increasingly cutting through their property during peak summer months. The situation has escalated to the point where residents are regularly contacting police to address the problem.

Colony resident Lori Hill described the challenges her community faces. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." Hill noted that when the fence was in place, property lines were clearly marked and confrontations were rare. Since its removal, residents have experienced repeated incidents of trespassing. "We used to confront them and tell them this is private property, and they would get pretty rude," Hill said. "So, now what we've just been doing is just calling the police, and they've been coming up and confronting them."

The matter was brought to the Juno Beach Town Council, where officials clarified that the town has no obligation to install a fence. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring more affordable alternatives. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. Not all beachgoers perceive the situation as problematic. Michael House, a visitor who regularly accesses JB-7 from a nearby public parking lot, said he has not witnessed the trespassing issues described by residents. "There's plenty of free parking. If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue," House said. "I have never noticed anyone hopping the fence or the shrubs or anything like that."

Hill expressed hope that the town will help resolve the dispute. "We're really hoping that the town will get back on board and just put it back up, so that we can have our landscaping and our private parking," Hill said. The town council indicated it will address the fence question during budget discussions scheduled for July 15. A potential fence replacement could cost the town thousands of dollars, making cost considerations central to the council's decision.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of just 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city. "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars," Lawson said. City leaders emphasized their long-term effort to revitalize the city and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," Miller-Anderson said. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive 'A' rating from state
cards.teaser: For the third year in a row, the School District of Palm Beach County received an 'A' rating from the state, continuing a streak district leaders say reflects strong student performance across all grade levels.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the state for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, received "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate, with 86% of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach delivered one of the district's biggest success stories, jumping from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has led the school for 15 years, spearheaded the turnaround by modifying the early childhood curriculum program for students starting at age 3. The school had earned an "A" rating two years prior before narrowly missing a "B" the previous year. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating this year, alongside Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade and will be representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
While most people will be relaxing this holiday weekend, the Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials get invited to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledges the magnitude of the moment, noting that millions, if not billions, of people will be watching. "It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion," she said. Senior Stephin Restivo emphasized the team's focus on precision, saying "Everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of." Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, stating "I have full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." For senior Lily Schaffer, the invitation demonstrates the program's growth. "Getting to do this is an amazing opportunity. It shows how much we've grown and showcases what we do here, because this program is so amazing," she said. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those cheering from home.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football eyes state title run after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots are preparing for the 2026 fall football season with sights set on a state title after finishing last season with a 10-2 record and a district title.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are targeting a state title run after finishing last season with a 10-2 record and a district championship. A second-round playoff exit, however, left the team believing more was achievable. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the senior class are four-year players who came through the middle school program. "They know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

With a veteran senior class leading the way, Saint Andrew's is embracing a more demanding schedule for the 2026 fall season. Senior Jack Williams said the program wanted to elevate to the next level by competing against quality teams. For the Scots, measuring success comes down to one metric: advancing further in the postseason. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that going undefeated in the regular season means nothing if the team continues losing in the second round of the playoffs. "We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters," Whelche said. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the team is using summer workouts as motivation, with daily effort building toward positive results when the season begins.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied reconstruction surgery coverage hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to the denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that GalaFlex's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined." Anthem responded to Clark's case by saying the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval, though the company noted Clark retained the right to appeal the decision.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is less risky than other options with proven success. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Last year, after investigative reporting shared breast cancer patients' stories of denial, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. A new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act to protect breast cancer patients from being denied treatments during their cancer journeys.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year
cards.teaser: According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation, with ground beef up 5.5% and buns up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%, while ice cream prices have risen 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive this year. Potato prices are down, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch offered strategies to manage costs: "It's really important to shop savvier than ever, it is comparing the stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list, the biggest thing for families is cutting down the food waste, and that begins with a meal plan," Woroch said.
